title: Org Constitution
lifecycle: Versioned — major review yearly, minor updates anytime
trigger: New organisation standards or yearly review cycle
doel: Establish the baseline coding, security, and process standards that every project must follow or explicitly override.
outputs: System prompt context for AI agents across all projects
note: Project constitutions can override specific sections by explicitly declaring an override. Silent conflicts are not allowed.

aiTasks.name: Standards Completeness Checker
aiTasks.objective: Verify the org constitution covers all mandatory governance areas.
aiTasks.prompt: You are an Enterprise Architect. Review this org constitution for completeness: coding standards, security baseline (OWASP alignment), data protection, quality gates, tooling defaults, AI guidance. Flag missing sections with suggested content.

aiTasks.name: Security Baseline Reviewer
aiTasks.objective: Assess the security section against OWASP SAMM Level 1.
aiTasks.prompt: You are a Security Engineer. Review the security section against OWASP SAMM Level 1. Identify missing practices, outdated recommendations, and practices too vague to enforce. Output a gap analysis with recommended additions.

title: Project Constitution
lifecycle: One-time — versioned when major tech decisions change
trigger: Project start or adoption of a new tech stack
doel: Define project-specific standards (tech stack, conventions, tooling) that extend or override the org constitution.
outputs: Single source of truth for project conventions
note: AI agents should receive this document as system context. Project overrides must explicitly reference the org constitution section they override.

aiTasks.name: Stack Validator
aiTasks.objective: Validate tech stack consistency and flag EOL versions or missing layers.
aiTasks.prompt: You are a Solution Architect. Review this project constitution: (1) Are technology choices compatible? (2) Are any versions EOL or approaching EOL? (3) Are monitoring, CI/CD, and feature flags covered? (4) Does the stack match team skills? Output a risk table per technology choice.

title: PRD
trigger: Decision to build a new product or major feature
doel: Formally capture the initiative, scope, and business objective as the starting point for discovery.
note: The PRD is an entry gate, not a living document. After sign-off, epics and stories become the source of truth.

aiTasks.name: Scope Validator
aiTasks.objective: Validate PRD completeness and flag scope creep risks.
aiTasks.prompt: You are a Senior Product Manager. Review this PRD: (1) Is the problem statement specific and measurable? (2) Are success metrics SMART? (3) Is out-of-scope explicit? (4) Are assumptions documented? Output PASS/WARN/FAIL per section with improvements.

aiTasks.name: Stakeholder Impact Analyst
aiTasks.objective: Identify affected stakeholder groups and flag adoption risks.
aiTasks.prompt: You are a Change Manager. Identify all stakeholder groups impacted by this PRD. For each: impact level (H/M/L), likely concerns, and recommended engagement strategy. Flag any group not mentioned but who should be involved.

aiTasks.name: Multi-Stakeholder Requirements Review
aiTasks.objective: Review PRD requirements from business, user, and technical perspectives to find conflicts and gaps.
aiTasks.prompt:
You are running a multi-stakeholder review of this PRD. Three reviewers read it independently and respond.

**Reviewer 1 — Business Sponsor / Executive**
Do the stated goals map to measurable business outcomes? Is the scope proportional to the business value? What success looks like in 6 months? What's missing that a board would ask about?

**Reviewer 2 — End User Representative**
Does this PRD describe something you'd actually want to use? Which goals feel abstract rather than practical? What daily workflow does this improve — and is that clearly stated? What's described that you didn't ask for?

**Reviewer 3 — Solution Architect / Tech Lead**
Are the scope boundaries realistic? Are there requirements that will drive disproportionate technical complexity? Are NFRs (performance, security, scale) implicit but unstated? What's underspecified?

---
**Common Ground & Synthesis**
1. Which requirements all three reviewers support? These are your stable core.
2. Which requirements only one reviewer cares about? Flag for priority discussion.
3. Where do reviewers conflict? List the tension and recommend a resolution.
4. What's missing from the PRD that 2+ perspectives need?
5. Overall verdict: Proceed to discovery / Clarify first / Rethink scope.

title: Stakeholder Map
lifecycle: Living — updated when new stakeholders are identified
trigger: Project start or new stakeholder identified
doel: Provide clarity on who has which interests so that communication and reviews are correctly targeted.
outputs: Basis for interview planning in discovery
template:
# Stakeholder Map

## Stakeholders
| Name | Role | Interest | Influence | Availability |
|---|---|---|---|---|

## Power-Interest Grid
```
High power │ Keep satisfied  │ Manage closely
           │                 │
 Low power │ Monitor (low)   │ Keep informed
           ├─────────────────┴──────────────
           Low interest       High interest
```

## RACI Summary
| Deliverable | Responsible | Accountable | Consulted | Informed |
|---|---|---|---|---|

## Communication Plan

|---|---|---|---|

aiTasks.name: Interview Planner
aiTasks.objective: Generate tailored interview questions per stakeholder group.
aiTasks.prompt: You are a Senior Business Analyst. Based on this stakeholder map, generate 5-8 targeted interview questions per stakeholder group. Uncover: unstated requirements, constraints, political sensitivities, success criteria. Format as a table: Stakeholder Group | Questions.

aiTasks.name: RACI Generator
aiTasks.objective: Generate a RACI matrix for the key project deliverables.
aiTasks.prompt: You are a Project Manager. Based on this stakeholder map, generate a RACI matrix for the main project phases and deliverables. Flag roles with unclear accountability.
